_comment: The canonical check report: one complete example of the shape docs/spec.md
Contract 2 describes, carrying every field at once so there is one place to
read the contract off rather than six hand-written copies that drift.
This is the envelope a check sub-agent returns, not what `sniff.py` prints.
Each entry of `runs[]` is one `sniff.py run` or `sniff.py detonate` report
verbatim; the sub-agent adds `check`, its own per-check fields, and the
`derived`, `sensors` and `truncated` roll-ups over every run.
The values are deliberately not all clean: a hard rule trips, a cap cuts, a
sensor is down. A fixture where nothing happened does not exercise any of
the code that reads it. Conformance tests in all three consumers load this
file -- sandbox/tests/test_contract.py, apps/cujo and apps/web -- so a field
added on one side and forgotten on another fails somewhere.
Every block here carries every key it can, which is the maximal shape and
the reason this file is worth reading. The contract is looser than the
example in the envelope's three roll-ups and nowhere else, because those
three are the only blocks a sub-agent writes by hand rather than copying
from `sniff.py`. In `sensors`, `armed` is required and `detail` is not:
`armed` is the half `unarmedSensors` rules on, and `detail` is prose a
reader can already find quoted in the runs below. In `derived` and
`truncated`, every key is optional, though each key present must still be a
boolean and the block itself must still be an object -- the rules read the
top level and every `runs[]` entry, so a roll-up nobody wrote hides no
signal (decision 96). Inside `runs[]` nothing is loose: those blocks are
copied from `sniff.py`, and a key missing there means the producer moved.
